extracted.intended_audience: TeX / LaTeX users (beginners) who want to create high-quality vector graphics with MetaPost
extracted.subtask_description: Creating high-quality, scalable vector figures with MetaPost for inclusion in TeX/LaTeX documents, aimed at beginners who need practical guidance on commands, labels, colors, transforms, and inclusion workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce vector EPS graphics for scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Encapsulated PostScript (EPS) graphics are the most common types used because of their scalability; EPS can be scaled to any resolution without loss in quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPS can also be converted to raster formats (PNG, JPEG) or other vector formats (PDF, SVG). Use MetaPost to generate EPS output so figures remain high-quality when scaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: MetaPost source file structure and compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical MetaPost source file consists of one or more figures delimited by beginfig(i)...endfig; running mpost foo.mp yields one output file per figure (foo.1 .. foo.n) and a transcript log.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep each figure in a beginfig/endfig block; check foo.log for compilation messages. Expect n output files written: foo.1 .. foo.n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts are not embedded in MetaPost EPS output
rubrics_metrics.description: These EPS graphics are not self-contained in that fonts used in labels are not embedded into the graphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because fonts aren't embedded, use TeX/LaTeX for typesetting labels (escape to TeX) so labels match document fonts and render correctly when included in LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use btex ... etex to typeset labels with TeX/LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: The btex ... etex block instructs MetaPost to process everything in between using TeX (or LaTeX if configured), enabling high-quality typeset labels inside figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For LaTeX processing, include a verbatimtex preamble with '%&latex' and a minimal documentclass, e.g. verbatimtex %&latex \documentclass{minimal} \begin{document} etex before your beginfig. Example: label(btex $f(x)=x^2$ etex,(a,b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Label placement and justification suffixes
rubrics_metrics.description: By default label(string,point) centers the label; use suffixes (.lft, .rt, .bot, .top, .llft, .ulft, .lrt, .urt) to align labels relative to the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: label.top(btex A etex,(0,0)); places A directly above (0,0). Use appropriate suffix for readable, non-overlapping labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose draw vs fill appropriately for paths and closed cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: draw is used to draw paths or pictures; fill is used to fill closed paths (cycles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To draw straight segments: draw z1--z2--z3; to draw smooth Bézier curves: draw z1..z2..z3;. To fill a closed curve, append --cycle and use fill p withcolor <color>; combine fill and draw to show outlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer constructing holes by p--reverse q--cycle over fill+unfill for correct transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Using fill p then unfill q can produce improper transparency when placing the figure on a non-white background; instead use fill p--reverse q--cycle withcolor <color>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfill is equivalent to fill q withcolor background (background defaults to white), but p--reverse q--cycle traverses p then the reverse of q and ensures proper transparency on arbitrary backgrounds. Redefining background is possible but the reverse-cycle method is simpler and more robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control path tangents and smoothness using dir and brace syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dir, {right}, {up}, or {dir θ} attached to path points to force outgoing and incoming directions of the Bézier curve (e.g., draw z1{right}..z2{dir 45}..{up}z3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To require different incoming and outgoing directions at a point, use z2{dir θi}z2{dir θo} (specify incoming θi and outgoing θo). This constrains the Bézier curve's tangents for precise shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand path representation as cubic Bézier curves
rubrics_metrics.description: All paths in MetaPost are represented as cubic Bézier curves (piecewise cubic polynomials), which interpolate points and produce smooth paths; linear segments are a special case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fullcircle is a built-in path approximating a circle via Bézier curves (not true trig circle) but visually indistinguishable; use reverse, cycle, etc., to build complex closed paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pen data type for stroke properties and reuse pens
rubrics_metrics.description: The pen data type affects stroke properties; default stroke thickness is 0.5 bp and default unit is 1bp = 1/72 in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and store a pen variable with desired thickness to reuse across multiple stroked paths for consistent line widths in a figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Store reusable picture elements for animations or repeated drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: The picture data type stores an entire picture for later reuse so objects that remain the same across frames need not be redrawn manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use picture variables to hold static components when programmatically generating animation frames or when reusing a subfigure multiple times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use built-in affine transforms for shifts, rotations, scalings, slants
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost provides transformations (shift, rotation, horizontal/vertical scale, slant) as building blocks; combine them to produce rotated/scaled copies (e.g., build Figure 1 by rotating a circle multiple times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transform variables and operators to apply consistent transformations; combining transforms programmatically is efficient and precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify colors as (r,g,b) triplets and reuse color variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Colors are triplets in the unit cube (r,g,b) with components between 0 and 1; there are five built-in colors (black, white, red, green, blue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a color variable (e.g., bbblue:=(3/5,4/5,1);) if the color is used repeatedly. Use withcolor <color> in fill/draw commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow drawing: drawarrow and drawdblarrow accept any path
rubrics_metrics.description: drawarrow places an arrow head at the end of the path; drawdblarrow places arrow heads at both beginning and end. The path argument need not be straight segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can attach arrows to curved Bézier paths (e.g., drawarrow z1{right}..z2{dir 45}..{up}z3;) — arrowheads will be placed following the path's end tangent.

rubrics_metrics.name: When graphing functions: use the graph package or external data generators
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost's graph package (input graph;) can construct data and plot simple functions; for more complicated functions, generate data externally (MATLAB/Octave/Maple/Mathematica/Gnuplot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide graph size (e.g., begingraph(144bp,89bp);) then use gdraw "data.d"; consult the graph package manual for customization commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include MetaPost figures in LaTeX with graphicx and handle PDFLaTeX conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \includegraphics{foo.1} with the graphicx package. For PDFLaTeX, use ifpdf and \DeclareGraphicsRule to convert MetaPost graphics to PDF on-the-fly via mptopdf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example preamble: \usepackage{graphicx} \usepackage{ifpdf} \ifpdf \DeclareGraphicsRule{*}{mps}{*}{} \fi ; this allows PDFLaTeX to use Hans Hagen's mptopdf because PDFLaTeX cannot process PostScript directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the MetaPost previewer GUI for quick iteration and debugging
rubrics_metrics.description: A MetaPost previewer (graphical interface) can generate a single graphic, save output in EPS/PDF formats, save the source, and display the compilation log for debugging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the previewer to quickly test code snippets and inspect the log to fix compilation issues before producing final figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the nine MetaPost data types and use them appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost data types: numeric, pair, path, transform, color, string, boolean, picture, and pen — use them for storing numbers, points, Bézier paths, transforms, colors, text, booleans, whole pictures, and stroke properties respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pair for coordinates (x,y), numeric for scalars, path for Bézier curves, and string when reusing typeset labels. Structuring data appropriately simplifies code and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful that MetaPost is a programming language enabling flow control and automation
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost accommodates data structures and flow control; compilation of source code yields EPS graphics and its programming features allow automating repeated constructs (e.g., building animations without manual frame creation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use loops, variables, and stored pictures to programmatically generate families of figures or animation frames; consult the MetaPost manual for advanced constructs.
